Nvidia Reportedly Can Ship Only 1% of Chinese RTX Orders

China wants Nvidia chips. Nvidia can’t make enough.
Chinese AI and cloud firms, including Alibaba Group, Tencent Holdings and ByteDance, have ordered about 6 million Nvidia RTX Pro 5500 chips, according to Bloomberg. 

They expect to receive only some tens of thousands, roughly 1%, over the next four months.
The reason, per the report: Nvidia is struggling to boost production to meet soaring demand.

That’s a supply gap, not a demand problem. The article doesn’t say when production might catch up, or give a comment from Nvidia.

Is the bottleneck production, policy or both? And who fills the gap for Chinese AI developers while they wait?

🤖 One agent for everyone beats one agent per person, in all four of Anthropic's tests

Anthropic's alignment team put frontier models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Alibaba into shared-resource setups. Those included a token budget, a group food order and a merge queue. A single coordinator beat peer-to-peer agent teams by roughly 10 to 45 points for both Claude models.

On the shared API budget, Opus 5 teams hit just 47% of the coordinator's score, and Sonnet 5 teams hit 38%. Agents stalled as teams grew, overrode other users' requests and made unsupported claims about people.

Puttaparthi is Getting Decorated Again | Centenary Celebrations of Bhagawan Sri Sathya Sai Baba 2026

Gujarati New Year Celebrations | Devotional Music Program by Mr Prasan Rao, Ms Dhwani Muley & Team from Vadodara | Nov 10, 2026

With the divine blessings of Bhagawan Sri Sathya Sai Baba, the Gujarati New Year, celebrated as Bestu Varas or Saal Mubarak, was ushered in at Prasanthi Nilayam with a soulful musical offering by visiting artists and devotees from Gujarat.

The devotional music program was led by renowned vocalists Mr Prasan Rao and Ms Dhwani Muley, accompanied by Mr Kedar Singh Chauhan on keyboard, Mr Nirbhay Karekar on tabla, Mr Chandrakant Patel on talam and a chorus team.

The musical offering began with a touching tribute to Mother Eswaramma, followed by nostalgic compositions celebrating Bhagawan's divine life, His loving darshans and the bliss of His physical presence. Soulful prayers expressing love, longing and surrender to Sai were interspersed with compositions celebrating His advent in Parthi.

Adding a distinct Gujarati flavour, the artists presented a traditional devotional song in praise of Lord Shrinathji, beautifully connecting Gujarat's rich devotional heritage with the spiritual legacy of Puttaparthi. The repertoire also featured popular compositions dedicated to Lord Ganesha, Lord Krishna and Lord Rama, along with universal prayers honouring the great spiritual traditions of different faiths.

How Swami’s Grace Has Sustained and Shielded Me | Narayana Bhatta | Satsang from Prasanthi Nilayam

For Me,
Veda = God
Swami = Love

For Mr Narayana Bhatta, the Vedas are God. Born into a humble and deeply pious family, he was initiated into Vedic learning at a very young age by his father. The sacred flame kindled during those early years went on to become his lifelong source of strength, guidance, and wisdom.

Even as he pursued secular education and later rose to occupy senior positions in several banks, his commitment to Vedic study, chanting, and teaching remained unwavering. Little did he realise then that this sincerity, devotion, and purity of purpose would one day bring him face to face with the love of his life, Bhagawan Sri Sathya Sai Baba.

At a most opportune moment in his life, Swami drew him close and bestowed upon him the rare and priceless blessing of serving as a priest at Prasanthi Nilayam. Those four to five years remain among the most cherished and golden moments of his life.

In this Satsang, Mr Bhatta offers a glimpse into his remarkable spiritual journey, sharing how he has experienced the visible and invisible hand of God through more than seventy years of life. His inspiring narration is a testament to purity, perseverance, divine grace, and the transformative power of Pure Love.

🇷🇺On November 11, the Russian Ministry of Defense announced that two settlements, Shilovka in the DPR and Voskresenka in the Zaporozhye region, had come under the control of the Russian Armed Forces.

Shilovka is located on the northern bank of the Grishinka River, approximately 14 km west of the outskirts of Krasnoarmeysk (Pokrovsk) and 7 km from the administrative border between the DPR and the Zaporozhye region.

The "Vostok" group took control of Voskresenka and the surrounding areas. According to the Ministry of Defense, the settlement was occupied by servicemen of the 5th Separate Tank Brigade of the 36th Combined Arms Army.

Voskresenka is located on the eastern bank of the Verkhnyaya Tersa River, on the road between Barvinkovo and Novonikolaevka. Previously, the Russian Ministry of Defense reported the capture of Vasilykovo, located nearby.

The Ministry of Defense stated that during prolonged fighting for Voskresenka, Russian units occupied a fortified defensive area of the Ukrainian Armed Forces.

The claimed Ukrainian losses in this area amounted to up to a company of personnel, two armored vehicles, six cars, seven pieces of motor vehicles, 42 ground robotic complexes, and more than 50 heavy hexacopter drones of the "Baba Yaga" type.

Voskresenka is located in the area of advance of the "Vostok" group in the Zaporozhye region. Its capture expands the zone of Russian control and creates conditions for further offensive operations. An intermediate objective at this stage is to reach Novonikolaevka in order to physically cut off Zaporozhye from the Dnepropetrovsk direction and to try to develop a successful offensive in this area.
